details: CONFIRMED by running the branch's check_types against relay's real types-lint on a fresh UV_CACHE_DIR. Two causes:
(a) `if not out and running` drops the running tool whenever any probe failed, and on a cold cache the tool after the running
one is always uncached, since types_lint.py runs mypy then ruff in order; (b) a probe TimeoutExpired is read as "present",
while it means the tool's run is blocked, the same state that caused the timeout. The tests model "missing" only as a uv that
fails offline at once, a state the reported case does not reach (the download ends in seconds). The probes also stretch the
step past its budget by up to 40 s (35.1 s measured for a 15 s budget). The item's pass case "with mypy missing, precheck names
mypy" fails in the item's own scenario. Size: 30 min.
evidence: UV_CACHE_DIR=<fresh> python3 -I q.py <worktree> <copy of bin/types-lint, bin/types_lint.py, lib/x.py>   (STEP_TIMEOUT=15)
FAIL types and lint took longer than 15 s
ruff is not installed (not in the uv cache): run uv tool install ruff@0.13.3, or relay doctor
left behind: 42913 ppid 1 `uv tool run mypy==1.18.2 lib/x.py`
Cold-cache probe: `uv tool run --offline mypy==1.18.2 --version` started 8 s after the download: real 259.05, user 0.29
failing_case: Fresh uv cache (UV_CACHE_DIR empty, as in the sandbox), relay's real bin/types-lint and bin/types_lint.py, STEP_TIMEOUT 15.
types_lint.py runs mypy first: uv downloads it in seconds, then mypy's first run blocks for minutes. At the timeout
_running_tool finds mypy; the offline probe of mypy==1.18.2 then blocks too (mypy is in the cache, its first run hangs) and
hits its 20 s timeout, which the code counts as "present"; the probe of ruff@0.13.3 fails at once because types_lint.py never
reached ruff. Output now, after 35.1 s:
FAIL types and lint took longer than 15 s
ruff is not installed (not in the uv cache): run uv tool install ruff@0.13.3, or relay doctor
It should name mypy (the tool still running, or not yet usable) and its next step; ruff, not yet reached, is not the cause.
fix_hint: Report the running tool first and always (it is the cause the timeout saw); list only tools that come before or are the
running one as missing, or drop the offline probe for the running tool; read a probe timeout as "first run still blocked"
(say so), not as present. Cap the probes to a few seconds in total. Add a test where the running process is mypy and ruff's
offline probe fails: the lines name mypy and do not blame ruff.
pass_cases: 1. Cold cache, mypy downloaded but its first run blocks past the step budget, ruff not yet in the cache: the lines name mypy
(still running / first run of a fresh download) with a next step, and do not say "ruff is not installed" as the cause.
2. mypy not in the uv cache and uv tool run fails offline at once (the test's fake uv): the lines name mypy and
3. Both tools cached, the step hangs in ruff: "still running: ruff (ruff@0.13.3)" (the existing test keeps passing).
4. The extra diagnosis after a timeout takes at most a few seconds, not 20 s per tool (no probe that runs the blocked tool).
findings.summary: on the item's own case (cold uv cache) the timeout blames ruff as not installed and never names mypy, which was the tool running

details: CONFIRMED: timing probe on the branch and on master with the same script. communicate() reads to EOF, and EOF comes only when
every holder of the pipe's write end exits; kill() hits only bash. Relay's own types_lint.py captures uv's output on its own
pipes, so relay itself does not hang today, but the step's real work (uv and mypy) is orphaned and keeps loading the machine
that was already too slow. Fix both by starting the step in its own session and killing the group. Size: 15 min.
evidence: python3 -I p.py <branch> repo   -> ['FAIL types and lint took longer than 1 s'] 12.3 s
python3 -I p.py <master> repo   -> ['FAIL types and lint took longer than 1 s'] 1.0 s
ps after the fresh-cache run: 42913 ppid 1 /Users/amidman/.local/bin/uv tool run mypy==1.18.2 lib/x.py
failing_case: bin/types-lint is `sleep 12; echo done` (bash forks the child; the same for any types-lint that runs mypy without exec or
without capturing its output). STEP_TIMEOUT 1. Branch: check_types returns after 12.3 s (it waits for sleep to exit, so a
hung mypy hangs precheck for ever). master: 1.0 s, because subprocess.run on POSIX only calls wait() after kill().
The step's children also survive: with relay's real types-lint, `uv tool run mypy==1.18.2 ...` was left running with ppid 1
fix_hint: Popen(..., start_new_session=True); on timeout read the running tool, then os.killpg(proc.pid, SIGKILL) and proc.wait()
(or communicate with a short timeout), never an unbounded communicate().
pass_cases: 1. types-lint `sleep 12; echo done`, STEP_TIMEOUT 1: check_types returns in under 3 s with the timeout line.
2. Same script: after check_types returns, no process of the step (the sleep) is still alive.
3. types-lint `exec sleep 30` (the existing timeout tests): still the timeout line and the tool lines.
4. A types-lint that fails at once: "FAIL types and lint (bin/types-lint):" and its output tail, as today.
reason: tests/test_precheck.py:183 (killpg, returns quick, no child left) passes, fails at base; killpg verified by hand.
findings.summary: after the kill, proc.communicate() waits with no bound for any child still holding the output pipe; the 60 s bound is lost
